title: deployment-trajectory-heatmap-and-regression-explainer
creator: Priya Natarajan
description: Build a visual + analytic feature in Console that surfaces the "trajectory" of deployment health over time using a heatmap and automated regression explainer. The feature will help PMs, SREs, and engineers quickly decide whether to continue, pause, or rollback a gradual traffic shift (A/B, canary, shadow) by correlating metric drift with recent changes (model version, routing policy, infra events).
background: Current rollout pages show per-metric timeseries and cohort snapshots, but it is difficult to spot transient regressions that emerge during traffic ramps or to attribute a signal to a recent change. Support teams often need to manually stitch traces, logs, and config diffs when triaging. We want a single view that highlights where the deployment health diverges and provides a prioritized list of likely causes and immediate remediation suggestions (e.g., pause, narrow traffic slice, rollback).
goals: Surface a compact timeline heatmap (per-route + per-metric) that shows distributional shifts during a deployment window
Provide an automated regression explainer that ranks candidate causes (model diff, routing change, infra event, upstream latency) with confidence scores
Expose direct trace links and suggested rollback actions (safe rollback, partial rollback, pause) from the same view
Make the view queryable by route, search, and arbitrary time window; persist snapshots for postmortem analysis
acceptance_criteria: Heatmap renders for any deployment with >= 10k requests in selected window and supports median/p50-p99 buckets
Explainer returns top 3 candidate causes with supporting signals (correlation and delta) within 90s of data availability
UI shows direct links to sampled traces and the associated GitHub PRs or config diffs when available
Rollback action button triggers the existing rollout control flow (canary shrink / variant swap) with confirmation and audit log entry
Snapshots can be exported as a JSON report and attached to a deployment incident
engineering_notes: Backend: extend telemetry ingestion to compute per-route distribution deltas over sliding windows; store compact histogram summaries for fast heatmap rendering. Explainer: lightweight causal ranking that uses delta correlations + feature flags as candidates. UI: new panel under Deployments with time scrubber, heatmap, ranked causes, and trace/rollback widgets. Coordinate with ENG infra team for sampling and trace linking (ENG-9124).
rollout_plan: Alpha: expose to internal SREs and two pilot customers as an opt-in console flag. Beta: open to all internal teams and select customers. GA: enable by default with a single top-level Deployments -> Trajectory view. Track telemetry on usage and false-positive explainer feedback.
metrics: Mean time to detect deployment-impacting regression (target: -30%)
Fraction of rollbacks initiated from the Trajectory view (target: 20% of rollbacks)
Explainer precision@3 measured by post-deploy feedback (target: >= 70%)
Heatmap render latency (target: < 500ms for 90th percentile queries)
risks: False-positive explainer leads to unnecessary rollbacks — mitigate with conservative thresholds and user confirmation
Additional load on telemetry pipelines during heavy deployment activity — coordinate sampling and histogram aggregation
Sensitive customer data surfaced in explainers or snapshots — ensure masking and KMS-backed export controls
dependencies_notes: Requires ENG work on histogram summarization (ENG-9348) and trace-anchor APIs (ENG-9124). Design needs final accessibility review. We also depend on Console RBAC rules to surface rollback actions only to authorized users.
